{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from LSF)

# LSF requested:
#   -q gpuv100
#   -gpu "num=1:mode=exclusive_process"
#   -J NN_03-01
#   -o output/NN_03-01-%J.out
#   -n 5
#   -R "span[hosts=1]"
#   -R "rusage[mem=6GB]"
#   -W 20:00
#   -B
#   -N

flux alloc \
  -n 5 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --time=20h \
  --queue=gpuv100 \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p output

# Approximate LSF %J using Flux job id.
exec >"output/NN_03-01-${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>&1

# NOTE: LSF -R "rusage[mem=6GB]" (memory request) has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: LSF GPU mode=exclusive_process has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: without exclusive GPU-mode enforcement, you may contend with other processes on the same GPU
# (site-dependent), causing performance variability.

# NOTE: LSF -R "span[hosts=1]" (single-host placement) has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: tasks may be distributed across hosts depending on site policy, which can affect performance.

# NOTE: LSF email notifications (-B/-N) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive start/end emails.

# NOTE: LSF job name (-J NN_03-01) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

module purge
module load tensorflow/1.5-gpu-python-3.6.2

for drop in 0.2 0.25 0.3 0.4
do
	for N in 250 350 400 450 550
	do
		for nhidden in 6
		do
			for act in sigmoid
			do
				for folder in "03-01-2019 11.04" "09-01-2019 12.57" "11-10-2018 11.36"
				do
					for func in group_period_x_group_period group_period_2x2 atomic_number
					do
						python3 NN/NN_script.py $drop $N sigmoid 6 "$folder" $func
					done
					done
				done
		done
	done
done
'
"
}
